approved_note: Drafted by Claude on 7 Oct 2026. Approved by Noemi on 7 Oct 2026, including the eight calls that were marked for her: q04, q05, q10, q13, q15, q20, q24 and q30.

cases.text: gentle exfoliant for sensitive skin under £30
cases.notes: The brief's own example, word for word. 'gentle' is a wish for the search terms, not a must-have.

cases.text: moisturiser for dry + sensitive skin, fragrance free pls, 15-25 quid
cases.notes: UK spelling, two skin types joined by '+', slang 'quid' -> GBP, a range with the currency word after it. 'fragrance free' normalised to 'fragrance-free'.

cases.text: spf 50 sunscreen for oily skin no white cast under $20
cases.notes: SPF and price in one request: 50 is the SPF, 20 is the budget. Trap: swapping them, or reading 50 as a budget.

cases.text: niacinamide serum for combo skin w breakouts, around 15 euros
cases.notes: 'combo' -> combination, 'breakouts' -> acne-prone, 'around 15' -> max 15, 'euros' -> EUR. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: the named ingredient is kept as a must-have rather than folded into product_type ('niacinamide serum').

cases.text: retinol for mature skin, max 40€
cases.notes: Currency symbol after the number. 'retinol' maps to the generic 'retinoid'. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: whether 'retinol' should also be kept as a must-have, since the shopper named that specific form (prescription retinoids like tretinoin would not fit).

cases.text: fragrance free clenser for oily acne prone skin, cerave or similar, under 12.50
cases.notes: Typo 'clenser'. Budget with a decimal and no currency: currency must be null, never guessed. Trap: the brand 'cerave or similar' is a hint for search, not a must-have.

cases.text: need an eye cream 15ml max £35
cases.notes: Size and price side by side with no punctuation: 15 is millilitres, 35 is the budget.

cases.text: lip balm that actually fixes cracked lips, less than 5 dollars
cases.notes: Currency as a word ('dollars' -> USD), 'less than' -> max. 'cracked lips' is the problem to solve (search terms), not a skin type or must-have.

cases.text: toner w/o alcohol for combination/normal skin €10-€20
cases.notes: Range with the symbol on both numbers. Two skin types joined by a slash. 'w/o alcohol' normalised to 'alcohol-free'.

cases.text: daily moisturizer w spf30+ for dry skin, 1.7 fl oz, $25 or less
cases.notes: US spelling, three numbers (SPF 30, 1.7 fl oz, $25). 'spf30+' -> 30. One need, not two: a moisturiser that has SPF (compare q27). confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: product_type 'moisturiser' rather than 'sunscreen'.

cases.text: mineral sunscreen spf 30 for sensitve skin between 20 and 30 pounds
cases.notes: Typo 'sensitve'. The number 30 appears twice, once as SPF and once as the top of the budget. 'pounds' here is money (GBP), not weight.

cases.text: electric kettle that lasts 10+ years
cases.notes: The brief's own example, word for word. No budget stated, so no budget key: 10 is years, not money.

cases.text: 1.7l kettle under £40
cases.notes: Size and price together: 1.7 litres, max £40. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: plain 'kettle' read as electric (the UK default, and 1.7l is the standard electric size) rather than asking which kind.

cases.text: 210mm gyuto for a beginner, around $100
cases.notes: Enthusiast word 'gyuto' (the Japanese chef knife) maps to 'chef knife'. 210 is blade length in mm, 100 is the budget; 'around' -> max. 'for a beginner' is context, not a must-have.

cases.text: 10 inch cast iron skilet that'll last 20+ yrs, under 50 bucks
cases.notes: Typo 'skilet'. Three numbers: 10 inches (size), 20 years, 50 budget. 'inch' -> 'in', 'yrs' -> years. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: slang 'bucks' read as USD, in line with the dollars -> USD rule (it could also mean other dollars).

cases.text: 28cm frying pan, non stick but pfas free, £30-60
cases.notes: Range with the symbol only on the first number: both ends are GBP. 28 is the size in cm, not money. Two must-haves.

cases.text: 2qt stainless steel saucepan, dishwasher safe, up to 80 usd
cases.notes: Unit glued to the number ('2qt'). Currency code written as a lowercase word ('usd'). 'up to' -> max. 'dishwasher safe' -> 'dishwasher-safe'.

cases.text: enameled dutch oven 5.5 quart, from 100 to 200 euro
cases.notes: 'quart' normalised to 'qt', decimal size. 'from X to Y' is a range, not a min only. Singular 'euro' -> EUR. Must-have kept in the shopper's US spelling.

cases.text: espresso machine w a proper steam wand, willing to spend at least €400
cases.notes: A minimum budget only ('at least' -> min, no max). Trap: reading 400 as a maximum.

cases.text: burr grinder for pour over, 150 or less, im in the uk
cases.notes: 'burr grinder' -> coffee grinder with 'burr' as a must-have; 'pour over' is a use for the search terms. Trap: no currency is written, so currency is null even though the shopper says they are in the UK. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: whether a stated country should set the currency (GBP) or stay null under the never-guess rule.

cases.text: glass teapot w infuser for loose leaf, no plastic, about 25 quid
cases.notes: 'about' -> max, 'quid' -> GBP. 'no plastic' normalised to 'plastic-free'. 'loose leaf' is a use, not a must-have.

cases.text: stovetop kettle that works on induction, whistling, $29.99 max
cases.notes: Decimal price with 'max' after it. Stovetop, not electric (contrast q12 and q13). 'works on induction' -> 'induction-compatible'.

cases.text: something nice for my mum
cases.notes: The brief's vague-need example. No category and no product: ask what kind of thing, don't guess.

cases.text: need something for my skin its been really dry lately
cases.notes: Vague but the category is clear and a skin type is hinted. Trap: guessing 'moisturiser'. Ask which product they want. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: clarify rather than ok with moisturiser for dry skin.

cases.text: kitchen stuff for my first flat, budget £200
cases.notes: Vague even though a category word and a budget are given: no product type. Trap: a budget makes it look ready to search.

cases.text: a kettle and a good chef knife under £100 total
cases.notes: Two different needs in one request, both kitchen. Ask which to start with. Trap: the shared budget makes it read like one request.

cases.text: sunscreen and a moisturizer for combo skin, under $40 each
cases.notes: Two skincare needs ('and', 'each'). Contrast with q10, where a moisturiser with SPF is one need. Ask which one first.

cases.text: best laptop for uni under 800
cases.notes: The brief's out-of-scope example, with a budget added. Trap: a parsable budget is no reason to accept it; reply with a polite no.

cases.text: hair dryer that wont fry my curls under £100
cases.notes: Near-miss: sounds beauty-ish, but hair tools are haircare, not skincare, and none of the skincare subreddits cover it.

cases.text: quiet dishwasher for a small kitchen
cases.notes: Near-miss: says 'kitchen', but a dishwasher is a large built-in appliance, not the cookware, knives, coffee and tea gear our kitchen subreddits cover. confirmed by Noemi, 7 Oct 2026: large appliances are out of scope for 'kitchen gear'.
